answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a costly, nontransferable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, independently verified task exposes fraud. The stake does not prove a unique human; it makes multiplying identities expensive, because every sybil must tie up capital and risk forfeiture. Set the bond above the expected gain from manipulating a market, and a fake-agent swarm must pay more in locked funds and penalties than it can extract. A ledger can label the rule onyx, its entry point jetty, and the audit pool reef—names, not security.
